subject: data-entry
title: Model Question Paper 1
meta: Time: 2 hours · Maximum marks: 40 · Modelled on the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: All questions are compulsory. Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Section A: questions 1–7 are MCQs (1 mark each); questions 8–10 have two parts of 1 mark each (assertion–reason, fill in the blanks, true/false); questions 11–17 carry 1 mark each.
Section B: 2-mark answers in 30–50 words, 3-mark answers in 50–80 words, the 4-mark answer in 80–120 words.
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: What are utility software? Give examples.
questions.answer: Utilities are system software that bridge the gap between the operating system and the needs of users. Examples: compress (zip)/uncompress (unzip) software, antivirus software, and split and join files software.

questions.q: Differentiate between copying text and moving text.
questions.answer: Copying makes a copy of the selected text and puts it in another place, leaving the original unchanged (Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V). Moving (cutting) removes the selected text from its place and inserts it in another place (Ctrl+X, Ctrl+V).

or.q: Write the steps to move a line of text from one place to another.
or.answer: (1) Select the line of text. (2) Click Cut in Home → Clipboard or press Ctrl+X. (3) Place the cursor where the text should go. (4) Click Paste or press Ctrl+V. (Or drag the selection with the mouse and drop it in the new place.)

questions.q: How do you hide and unhide a worksheet?
questions.answer: Hide: right-click the sheet tab and choose Hide. Unhide: right-click any visible sheet tab, choose Unhide, select the hidden sheet from the list and click OK.

questions.q: Differentiate between formulas and functions.
questions.answer: A formula is an expression written by the user, starting with =, using operators and cell references, e.g. =B3+C3+D3. A function is a built-in formula with a name, to which you give arguments in parentheses, e.g. =SUM(B3:D3) or =AVERAGE(B3:D3).

questions.q: What is the importance of a slide in a presentation?
questions.answer: Slides are the building blocks of a presentation. Each slide presents one idea with text, pictures, charts or media, helping the speaker present points in order and helping the audience understand and remember the message.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: What is the difference between system software and application software? Give examples.
questions.answer: System software runs and controls the computer and manages its resources; it works in the background and supports other programs — e.g. operating systems (Windows, Linux, UNIX) and utilities (antivirus, zip). Application software is written to do a specific task for the user — e.g. MS-Word for documents, MS-Excel for calculations, or a payroll package. Application software needs system software to run.

or.q: Differentiate between low-level and high-level languages with examples.
or.answer: Low-level languages are close to the machine: machine language (0s and 1s) and assembly language (mnemonics). They are machine dependent and hard to learn. High-level languages use English-like statements, are machine independent and easy to program, e.g. BASIC, COBOL, FORTRAN, C and C++. High-level programs need a compiler to be translated into machine language.

questions.q: Explain the purpose of Slides, Handouts and Notes Pages in the 'Print What' option of the Print dialog box.
questions.answer: Slides — prints one full-page slide on each page, e.g. for display. Handouts — prints several slides (2, 3, 6…) on each page to give the audience a summary. Notes Pages — prints one slide with its speaker notes on each page, for the speaker's use. (Outline View prints only the text outline.)

or.q: Explain Sentence case, Title case and Toggle case in the Change Case option.
or.answer: Sentence case — capitalises the first letter of the first word in each sentence. Title case (Capitalize Each Word) — capitalises the first letter of every word and makes the rest lowercase. Toggle case — the opposite of Title case: the first letter of every word lowercase and the remaining letters capital.

sections.title: Long answer question. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: What types of documents are required for mail merge? Write the steps for creating a data source in MS Word for mail merge.
questions.answer: Required documents: main document (fixed text), data source (changing information) and the merge document produced after merging. Steps to create a data source with the wizard: (1) Mailings → Start Mail Merge → Step by Step Mail Merge Wizard. (2) In step 3 (Select recipients) choose 'Type a new list' → Create. (3) Type the details in fields such as Title, First Name, Last Name, Address, City. (4) Click New Entry for each record; use Customize Columns to add, delete or rename fields. (5) Click OK, give a file name and Save (.mdb).

or.q: What is mail merge? Explain its uses and write the steps to merge a letter with a data source.
or.answer: Mail merge produces personalised copies of a document for many people. Uses: form letters, labels, envelopes, directories, e-mails. Steps: (1) Mailings → Start Mail Merge → Letters. (2) Type the letter, leaving space for the address. (3) Select Recipients → Use Existing List (or Type New List). (4) Insert Address Block / merge fields. (5) Preview Results. (6) Finish & Merge → Print Documents or Edit Individual Documents.
